key_insight: Coupling source-only teacher calibration with target-domain student learning can strip away teacher bias in LLM distillation and recover the oracle student at a provable polynomial rate, even without target reward feedback.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical distillation recipe for domain-shifted deployment: use cheap source feedback to continuously recalibrate the teacher while training the student on target prompts, reducing reliance on labeled target rewards.
method: Calibrate the teacher on source questions using reward feedback only.
Train the student on target questions with the calibrated teacher via token-level branching.
Feed the updated student back into the next calibration step, forming a coupled iterative loop.
evidence_signal: The abstract gives a theoretical convergence guarantee: the student’s expected average KL divergence to the oracle student goes to zero polynomially in the number of iterations, and it contrasts this with a direct-matching baseline that can stay bounded away from zero.
watch_item: The guarantee is theoretical and depends on an autoregressive policy framework, projected gradient updates, and access to reliable source-domain reward feedback; performance may degrade if these assumptions fail in practice.
paper_title: Coupled Calibration and Learning: Mitigating Teacher Bias in LLM Distillation without Target-Domain Reward Feedback
